verdict.rationale: Fern's own Web Analytics tab reports llms.txt usage, including traffic broken down by LLM provider (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor). That gives AI-agent traffic visibility alongside the docs' regular web analytics. The documented split covers only llms.txt usage, not general page reads, so it is unclear whether agent and human readers are classified across all traffic. missing for 10: evidence that agent-vs-human segmentation applies to all page views (including .md fetches and MCP access), detail on how agents are detected and attributed, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my docs analytics distinguish AI-agent traffic from human traffic so I can see who — or what — is actually reading

citations.quote: The tab reports `llms.txt` usage including: Traffic by LLM provider (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.)
